comparator.name: Human Resource Studies: People Management
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-taught full-time People Management track requires sixty EC in each year. Its final year includes thirty open EC, Comparative Labor Relations in Europe, Social Philosophy, Cross-Cultural HRM and a twelve-credit thesis. The mobility window permits approved combinations of placement, minor and electives. The separate Dutch track has a different curriculum.
components: GROW mentoring and personal development continue across the programme and carry no credits.
Academic Skills for People Management A
The ordinary first-year binding study advice threshold is 42 EC.
Academic Skills for People Management B
Students must pass the SPSS skills test as well as the written examination to complete Causal Analysis Techniques.
Mobility Window: Approved Study or Internship
The 30 EC mobility window can contain approved study or an internship, including permitted combinations. Its subject content remains open in this comparison.
Bachelor’s Thesis in Human Resource Studies: People Management
Entry to the bachelor thesis requires 120 EC. This pathway earns those credits by the end of year two.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly identifies the English People Management track, which the current adopted Appendix I distinguishes from Dutch Personeelwetenschappen. No optional specialisation is selected.

core: International people management, strategic HRM and evidence-based organisational policy
Organisational psychology and sociological analysis of people, work and organisations
Talent, employee development, workplace health and well-being
Human-resource analytics, qualitative and quantitative research, causal analysis and evidence-based consulting
International labour relations, cross-cultural HRM and the social and economic dimensions of work
adjacent: International organisations, European employment institutions and cross-cultural workforce governance
questions: How can international organisations balance employee well-being, development and performance?
How can analytics and research improve evidence-based people-management decisions?
How do cultural and European institutional contexts shape labour relations and workforce policy?

candidates.label: Workplace psychology, well-being and talent development
International labour relations and workforce governance

selection.assessment: The closest option addresses organisational behaviour, evidence-based decisions and strategic and financial context. The second develops psychological health and development; the third develops institutions and policy affecting organisations and work. These are different curricular priorities, with each pair exceeding the four-course floor. No fourth option is considered.

alternatives.label: People, organisations & international business
alternatives.labelReason: Study people and organisational decisions in an international business setting. Combine organisational psychology, leadership, negotiation and social research with accounting, economics and digital strategy.
alternatives.concept: Study people and organisational decisions in an international business setting. Combine organisational psychology, leadership, negotiation and social research with accounting, economics and digital strategy.
progression: Checked all current offerings and formal prerequisites. Research methods precedes negotiation and organisational psychology; introductory economics precedes advanced economics. Brain and behaviour foundations precede health and clinical psychology where selected.

alternatives.label: Psychology, health & people at work
alternatives.labelReason: Study the psychological foundations of behaviour, health, stress and development, and apply social research and leadership to people at work. Business and economic courses provide a complementary organisational setting.
alternatives.concept: Study the psychological foundations of behaviour, health, stress and development, and apply social research and leadership to people at work. Business and economic courses provide a complementary organisational setting.
progression: Checked all current offerings and formal prerequisites. Research methods precedes negotiation and organisational psychology; introductory economics precedes advanced economics. Brain and behaviour foundations precede health and clinical psychology where selected.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the first option, this option gives sustained space to psychopathology, health, development, psychological assessment and evidence synthesis, rather than digital strategy, international business and public economics.

alternatives.label: International institutions, work & organisations
alternatives.labelReason: Study how international institutions and economic rules shape organisations and work. Combine EU and international law, political institutions and public policy with economics, organisational psychology, negotiation and social research.
alternatives.concept: Study how international institutions and economic rules shape organisations and work. Combine EU and international law, political institutions and public policy with economics, organisational psychology, negotiation and social research.
progression: Checked all current offerings and formal prerequisites. Research methods precedes negotiation and organisational psychology; introductory economics precedes advanced economics. Brain and behaviour foundations precede health and clinical psychology where selected.
alternatives.distinctness: This option prioritises political institutions, rights, international and EU law, policy analysis and political economy. The others give more weight to leadership practice or psychological health and development.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

uses design thinking to identify needs and develop a venture concept and prototype
designs empirical studies and uses surveys, sampling and introductory statistics
applies leadership theories, emotional intelligence and reflective planning to group and personal development
analyses leaders’ communication and develops advice from interviews and rhetorical practice
uses a supervised survey project to study emotion regulation, belonging and inclusive leadership
examines behaviour, teams, culture and change and synthesises evidence about organisational practice
uses simulations to study bargaining, power, framing and collaborative decision-making

blocks: Both address survey design, psychological measurement and analysis; UCR uses leadership and social-experience applications.
Both study psychological processes in organisations, including motivation, teams, leadership and culture.
Both introduce sociological theories and apply them to social life.
Both develop qualitative design, data collection and interpretation.
Both examine social influence, group behaviour and social psychological research.
Both develop statistical analysis for social and behavioural data.
Both study stress, health behaviour and well-being; UCR focuses on health and illness more broadly than the workplace.
Both address financial and management-accounting decisions; UCR does not specialise in personnel costs.
Both teach empirical design, operationalisation, measurement and introductory analysis.
Both introduce economic reasoning about markets and economic decisions.

Both use linear regression, statistical assumptions and empirical analysis. Tilburg also covers ANOVA, path analysis and logistic regression; UCR adds instrumental variables and economic applications.
Both address organisational strategy; UCR emphasises digital transformation.

notes.text: Tilburg integrates specialist study in strategic HRM, talent, work and health, research and consulting, followed by European labour relations, cross-cultural HRM and a required thesis. The UCR options combine related organisational, psychological and institutional study. They do not reproduce the full specialist people-management sequence.

audience.programmeDescription: Human Resource Studies: People Management at Tilburg University studies people, work and organisations in an international and European setting. It connects organisational performance with employee well-being through psychology, sociology, economics and management.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study through people and international business, psychological health and development, or international institutions and organisations. Tilburg provides specialist sequences in HRM, talent management, people analytics, consulting and cross-cultural workforce decisions, alongside a required thesis.
